correctness.rationale: PASS: For delta>0,r>0 and h(u)=u^2 e^-u on u>=0 (0 otherwise), Q=h(t)+r h(t-delta). On 0<t<delta derivative=t(2-t)e^-t. After the second pulse x=t-delta,k=r exp(delta), derivative has sign of P=-(1+k)x^2+2(1+k-delta)x+delta(2-delta), with discriminant 4[k^2+(2-delta^2)k+1]. For delta>2, two additional simple positive roots occur iff k>(delta^2-2+delta sqrt(delta^2-4))/2, giving exact two-peak iff r>R(delta); boundary double-root is a shoulder, not second max. For delta<=2 one strict max including delta=2 equality. Log differentiation gives R prime/R=-1+2/sqrt(delta^2-4), hence strict rise to 2sqrt2, fall thereafter, and a genuine bimodal–unimodal–bimodal interval of fixed r between exp(-2) and peak. Independently reconstructed derivative polynomial, root criterion, phase examples delta=2.01/3/5 for r=1/5 using exact rational and high precision calculations; general proof is analytic.
